com.esignal.jstandard.event

Class StatusEvent

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.util.EventObject
      • com.esignal.jstandard.event.StatusEvent
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TurnAroundAware, java.io.Serializable
    Direct Known Subclasses:
    AnalyticsEvent, AuthTokenEvent, ConnectionEvent, ContentEvent, DictionaryEvent, HeadlineEvent, KeyLookupEvent, StoryEvent, SymbolEvent, TriggeredQuoteEvent

    public abstract class StatusEvent
extends java.util.EventObject
implements TurnAroundAware
    StatusEvent was introduced in order to provide status codes and descriptions. By default the status values will be SUCCESS (0) and ERROR (1). The status codes will improve over time depending on client needs and implementation complexities.

    In most cases the implementations e.g. DBCAPI should override the methods like getStatusString() and getStatusCode() in order to provide better understanding of the internal errors. Also, the implementation should provide a constants class which defines all possible error/success codes.

    Since:
    01-001-0010
    Author:
    Interactive Data Corporation
    See Also:
    Serialized Form

      • getStatusString

        public java.lang.String getStatusString()
        The String response should explain the internal problem in the form of String. This is useful in order to log/report status information.

        It is sometimes hard to code against every possible Status. This method is useful in the generalized scenario to show the client an internal status. 

         For example,
 if (getStatus() == DBCAPI.SUCCESS) {
   //do something
 } else if (getStatus() == DBCAPI_ERROR.INVALID_PARAM) {
   //Please check the required fields
 } else {
   //There was an internal error during processing, please report getStatusString() and getStatusCode() to support.
 }
        Returns:
        Implementation specific status represented as String.

      • getStatusCode

        public int getStatusCode()
        This method should be mapped with one-to-one with a constant class which represents all the error/success codes. This is useful in order to check conditions programmatically in order to stop execution or throw/catch Exceptions.

        It is sometimes hard to code against every possible Status. This method is useful while trying to show the client an internal code of status. 

         For example,
 if (getStatus() == DBCAPI.SUCCESS) {
   //do something
 } else if (getStatus() == DBCAPI_ERROR.INVALID_PARAM) {
   //Please check the required fields
 } else {
   //There was an internal error during processing, please report getStatusString() and getStatusCode() to support.
 }
        Returns:
        Implementation specific status represented as an int value.
